refnamediv.refpurpose: Sends a message to a socket, whether it is connected or not

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.parameters;
socket
The socket to send data to.
data
The data to be sent.
flags
Only STREAM_OOB (send out-of-band data) is used. Any other bit, such as STREAM_PEEK, is silently ignored. STREAM_OOB is not supported on a UDP socket, where the function returns -1. Over TCP, only the last byte of the data is urgent.
address
The address specified when the socket stream was created will be used unless an alternate address is specified in address. A UDP server socket created with stream_socket_server has no such address: without address, the function returns -1 and emits an E_WARNING. On a connected TCP socket, an alternate address is accepted and ignored.
If specified, it must be an address followed by a colon and the port, such as 127.0.0.1:9000; the address may be in square brackets, and IPv4 shorthand forms such as 127.1 are accepted. The port is mandatory, and any text after it is ignored.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns the number of bytes sent, as an integer,&return.falseforfailure;. The number can be smaller than the length of data, since the function does not loop until everything is sent. It is -1 if the send fails.

&reftitle.notes;
stream_socket_sendto writes straight to the socket, like stream_socket_recvfrom reads from it: it does not wait, so stream_set_timeout and default_socket_timeout do not apply and a blocking send on a full buffer may block indefinitely, whereas fwrite returns &false; after the timeout. Write filters are not applied, and on a stream with encryption enabled the data is sent unencrypted. Sending out-of-band data or data to an address on a filtered stream emits an E_WARNING and returns -1.
